## Example 6.8 · Parts (a–b) {#iv6-example-6-8-ab .vector-lesson .magnitude-lesson .angles-lesson .a-dense}

```{=html}
<p>Three points <span data-math="P"></span>, <span data-math="Q"></span> and <span data-math="R"></span> have position vectors <span data-math="\mathbf p"></span>, <span data-math="\mathbf q"></span> and <span data-math="\mathbf r"></span> respectively, where</p><div class="a-eq"><span data-math="\mathbf p=7\underset{\sim}{i}+10\underset{\sim}{j},\quad\mathbf q=3\underset{\sim}{i}+12\underset{\sim}{j},\quad\mathbf r=-\underset{\sim}{i}+4\underset{\sim}{j}."></span></div><div class="a-cols "><div><p>a) Write down the vectors <span data-math="\overrightarrow{PQ}"></span> and <span data-math="\overrightarrow{RQ}"></span> and show that they are perpendicular.</p><div data-module="reveal-panel" class="a-reveal"><button class="toggle-panel" aria-pressed="false">Show (a)</button><div class="panel-answer" hidden><div class="a-eq"><span data-math="\overrightarrow{PQ}=\begin{bmatrix}3-7\\12-10\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-4\\2\end{bmatrix}"></span></div><div class="a-eq"><span data-math="\overrightarrow{RQ}=\begin{bmatrix}3-(-1)\\12-4\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}4\\8\end{bmatrix}"></span></div><div class="a-eq"><span data-math="\overrightarrow{PQ}\cdot\overrightarrow{RQ}=(-4)(4)+2(8)=0"></span></div><p>Both vectors are non-zero, so they are perpendicular.</p></div></div></div><div><p>b) Using a scalar product, or otherwise, find <span data-math="\angle PRQ"></span>.</p><div data-module="reveal-panel" class="a-reveal"><button class="toggle-panel" aria-pressed="false">Show (b)</button><div class="panel-answer" hidden><div class="a-eq"><span data-math="\overrightarrow{RP}=\begin{bmatrix}8\\6\end{bmatrix},\quad\overrightarrow{RQ}=\begin{bmatrix}4\\8\end{bmatrix}"></span></div><div class="a-eq"><span data-math="\overrightarrow{RP}\cdot\overrightarrow{RQ}=8(4)+6(8)=80"></span></div><div class="a-eq"><span data-math="|\overrightarrow{RP}|=10,\quad|\overrightarrow{RQ}|=4\sqrt5"></span></div><div class="a-eq"><span data-math="\angle PRQ=\cos^{-1}\!\left(\frac{80}{10(4\sqrt5)}\right)\approx26.57^\circ"></span></div></div></div></div></div>
```

<div class="booklet-cue">Booklet Section 6 · p. 47</div>

::: notes
Additional multi-step problem. In part (a), reversing both vectors gives QP and QR with common tail Q, so the triangle is right-angled at Q. In part (b), the vertex is R, requiring RP and RQ.
:::
